name: Idaho

law.name: Revised Uniform Athlete Agents Act (Idaho Code 54-48) without registration sections

covers_nil_agents: Yes. The act covers agents for endorsement deals (Idaho Code 54-4802). Idaho has no separate NIL agent law.
summary: No state license, but the act's contract and school-notice rules apply.
contract_warning: Warning to student athlete. If you sign this contract: (1) you may lose your eligibility to compete as a student athlete in your sport; (2) if you have an athletic director, within 72 hours after signing this contract or before the next scheduled athletic event in which you participate, whichever occurs first, both you and your athlete agent must notify your athletic director that you have entered into this contract and provide the name and contact information of the athlete agent; and (3) you may cancel this contract within 14 days after signing it. Cancellation of this contract may not reinstate your eligibility as a student athlete in your sport.

steps.detail: Idaho's act has no registration. The contract and notice rules still apply.

steps.text: Register with each school's compliance office, if it asks
steps.detail: Most schools have their own agent sign-up.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director before you first contact the athlete
steps.detail: Send it in writing. If the athlete reached out first, tell the athletic director within 10 days.

steps.text: Use a written contract with all required items
steps.detail: Your pay and how it's figured, any other pay you get for the deal, anyone else being paid, expenses, services, length and date signed.

steps.text: Put the warning to student athlete in bold in the contract
steps.detail: Use the exact wording Idaho gives. If the athlete is a minor, change it to speak to the parent.

steps.text: Have the athlete sign a separate eligibility warning
steps.detail: It says signing may cost them their eligibility. If the athlete is a minor, the parent or guardian signs it instead.

steps.text: Give the athlete a copy when they sign
steps.detail: Give them the contract and the signed eligibility warning.

steps.text: Tell the athletic director in writing within 72 hours of signing
steps.detail: Or before the athlete's next game, whichever comes first. The athlete must tell the athletic director too.

steps.text: Have a parent or guardian sign if the athlete is a minor
Let the athlete cancel within 14 days if they want
steps.detail: They cancel by telling you in writing. They don't owe you anything and keep what you gave them.

steps.text: If a signed athlete later enrolls at a school, tell its athletic director within 72 hours
steps.detail: The 72 hours start when you learn they enrolled.

steps.text: Date the contract the day it's signed
steps.detail: Idaho law and federal law (SPARTA) both ban pre-dating or post-dating it.
Names and addresses of clients, every contract, and what you spent to recruit each athlete.

steps.text: Never give gifts or money to recruit athletes or make false promises
steps.detail: No false promises. No gifts or money to the athlete before signing, or to anyone else to get them. Breaking this is a misdemeanor in Idaho.

watch_list.item: Federal Protect College Sports Act of 2026 (S.4668)
watch_list.status: Passed the Senate on Sept 28, 2026. The House is out until Nov 9 and leaders say it won't pass as-is. It dies if not enacted by Jan 3, 2027.
watch_list.impact: It would require every NIL agent to register in a state, cap agent fees at 5% of an endorsement deal and limit contracts to the athlete's eligibility.

review_notes: The warning text was read from Idaho Code 54-4810 through a summary tool. Compare it word for word with the official page before printing contracts.
